article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Morning Brief
article.dek: One game left in Week 7: Cowboys at Eagles tonight, no card on the board yet, and Barkley is the name to watch at inactive time.

items.headline: Tonight: Cowboys at Eagles, 8:15 p.m. ET
paragraphs: Week 7 comes down to one game. The Dallas Cowboys visit the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field tonight at 8:15 p.m. ET, and the app's QB row has both starters confirmed: Dak Prescott for Dallas, Tanner McKee for Philadelphia.

McKee makes his fourth start. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs and is on injured reserve, so McKee stays under center. He went 26-for-45 for 215 yards in Philadelphia's 25-14 loss to Carolina on Oct. 18.
Both teams come in at 2-4. The winner stays alive in the NFC East race; the loser drops to 2-5. That is the whole Monday board, and it is the only game the app still prices this morning.
items.takeaway: One game left in Week 7: Prescott vs. McKee at 8:15 p.m. ET, with Hurts out for the season.

items.headline: Injury roundup: Barkley is the open question, two Eagles receivers are out
paragraphs: Philadelphia ruled out receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), linebacker Nolan Smith (concussion) and defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen) on Saturday's final injury report.

Saquon Barkley is the one open name. He is listed as questionable with a hamstring injury after missing the last two games, but he practiced in full on Saturday and reports say he is expected to play. That is not settled until the inactive list lands, about 90 minutes before kickoff.

Also questionable for Philadelphia: linebacker Jonathan Greenard (ankle), linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle), guard Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral), tight ends Grant Calcaterra (back) and Eli Stowers (quad), and cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee). Tight end Dallas Goedert carries no designation after a full Saturday practice and says he expects to play.
For Dallas, tackle Drew Shelton, receiver KaVontae Turpin and linebacker Dee Winters are ruled out, while receiver George Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. carry no designation.
items.takeaway: Smith and Wicks are out, Barkley is questionable but expected to play, and his call lands with tonight's inactives.

items.headline: Weather: clear and cool in Philadelphia tonight
paragraphs: Tonight in Philadelphia: clear skies, about 61 degrees at the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, falling into the mid-50s through the game, rain chance around 2 percent, wind west around 5 mph.
That is a fact, not a totals edge. Nothing in it argues the total either way.
items.takeaway: Clear, cool and calm for kickoff in Philadelphia; judge the total on its own.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: No card on the board yet — and that is the app doing its job
paragraphs: This morning all three headline cards read NO_PLAY. Hit Rate, Balanced and Value each show nothing, because no offer on tonight's game satisfies that lane's contract right now.

Hit Rate is the pick that looks most likely to win. It forgoes value for win probability, and the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate. Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. Value is always the model's +EV play. When none of the three fires, the app stays quiet rather than forcing a play.

The gap to watch is still there. The model's expected margin for Cowboys at Eagles is -0.45, about a pick'em, while the market board has Dallas -4.5. When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, do not guess. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
If a card appears on the evening refresh, it will be on tonight's game only, since that is the only game left on the board.
items.takeaway: No card yet is not a broken app. The model-versus-market gap on Dallas -4.5 is the number to run through Check.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets
paragraphs: (Hypothetical example:) Imagine a game where 70 percent of the tickets are on the favorite, but only 40 percent of the money is. That means lots of small bets on the favorite, and fewer, bigger bets on the underdog.

What could it mean? Tickets count bets. Handle counts money. When they point different ways, the average bet on one side is much bigger than on the other. That split is worth noticing, but it is not proof of anything on its own. One book's split alone does not make a Fade.

How to apply it: when you see tickets and handle disagree, treat it as a question, not an answer. Check whether the line has moved with the money, then run your own price through Check and let the app tell you whether that version is worth betting.
items.takeaway: Tickets count bets, handle counts money — when they disagree, ask why before you act on either one.

items.headline: Overnight: the Monday numbers did not move
paragraphs: Cowboys at Eagles is unchanged from the evening edition. Dallas is still -4.5 at both books: -108 at DraftKings and -112 at FanDuel, with Philadelphia +4.5 at -112 and -108. The DraftKings total is still 43.5, and FanDuel still shows 44.5.

The moneyline has not moved either: Dallas -218 at DraftKings and -220 at FanDuel, with Philadelphia +180 and +184. The model's expected margin is -0.45 this morning, about a pick'em, just as it was last night. So the model-versus-market gap on Monday is the same gap it was yesterday.
The rest of the Week 7 board shows no market prices this morning, because those games are already played. Tonight's game is the only number left to move.
items.takeaway: Nothing moved overnight on Dallas -4.5 or the total — the Monday gap is the same gap as last night.

items.headline: The one timing note: inactives tonight, not a better number later
paragraphs: When the board has not picked up a move, or your book is not DraftKings or FanDuel, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One timing note, and only one: the thing worth waiting for is tonight's inactives, about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, because Barkley is the one genuinely open question left. If your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet now. Waiting for a hoped-for number lets it drift the wrong way too, and tonight's game kicks off tonight.
items.takeaway: Wait only for tonight's inactives on Barkley; a good number that Check approves now is the play.

items.headline: Tonight's job: one game, one Check
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, and today it holds just one game. Work that game properly: starters are confirmed, the injury picture is settled except Barkley, and the model-versus-market gap on Dallas -4.5 is the number to run through Check.

Check your book's line and price, not just the DraftKings or FanDuel number in this brief. If Check says bet on your price, that is your verdict. If it says no, no card in this brief changes that. And remember what a price means: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and staking choice.
items.takeaway: One game left: confirm Barkley at inactive time, run your own price through Check, and let that verdict decide.
